question: does the raw-paragraph layer lift product-path retrieval toward the harness's answer-bearing-unit recall (the retrieval precondition of the 0.797 -> >=0.8045 parity target)?
design: product write_text -> orchestrated query, 20 questions seed 17 (same selection as the C2 probe); base arm = MEMPLEX_RAW_PARAGRAPH_LAYER=0, raw arm = layer on; metric session-level gold recall@8.

results.base_cross_check: identical to the C2 probe's base arm on the same questions
results.raw_partial: 5/5 hit on the first five raw-arm questions before the run was halted

findings: Base arm (20/20 complete): recall@8 0.85, exactly reproducing the C2 probe's base arm on the same seeded questions - two independent runs agreeing.
Raw arm: 5/5 hits on the questions completed before the halt (directionally clean but n=5 is anecdote, not evidence).

The run was halted by a real defect the probe surfaced: a very large corpus backfill (hundreds of long texts through one MPS batch path) wedges the backend with 26 threads parked at zero CPU - the same v13.1-era failure signature. Fixed after the halt by clamping embed_query_batch (16-chunk, 8192-char cap); the full 20-question raw arm should re-run under the clamp.
honest_reading: The J-level 0.797 -> >=0.8045 acceptance is NOT yet discharged: the raw arm did not complete, and even at n=20 the recall CI (~+/-16pp) cannot resolve sub-pp J-level deltas. This probe measures the retrieval precondition only; the J-level parity run (product orchestrated query + answerer + judge, multi pool) remains the acceptance instrument and is now unblocked by the MPS clamp. Evidence level: E1 for the base arm and the defect; the raw-arm claim is directional.
